summary: Klaus Karttunen studied indology and linguistics at the University of Helsinki (BA 1971–1990) under Pentti Aalto, Maarit Kaimio, Henrik Zilliacus, Holger Thesleff, and Asko Parpola. He held posts at Helsinki, the Academy of Finland (1985), and Freiburg (1991–1995).
Klaus Mylius was an indologist who held academic posts at Leipzig University (~1966–1990), the University of Bayreuth (~1991–1992), and Goethe University Frankfurt (~1993).
Klaus Pinte is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke (~1995–2014, MA) and served there as a teaching assistant in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He served as Prof. Dr. at the University of Giessen (~1974–2003) and held a post at the University of Göttingen (~2003), where he succeeded Heinz Bechert in 2003.
Indologist Klaus Rüping studied under Paul Hacker (~1965–1969). He held a post as Doz. Dr. at the University of Münster.

Klaus Wille specializes in indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1985–2018), the University of Göttingen, and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Mathes studied under Klaus Sagaster, Michael Hahn (PhD, Marburg), and at Hamburg. He directed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1993), researched at Hamburg (2001), and became a professor at Vienna (~2010).
Klemens Karlsson specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at Uppsala University under the supervision of Peter Schalk (~1994–2000).

Knut A. Jacobsen studied religious studies and indology at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1990–1994). He served as a professor at the University of Oslo (~1994–1996) and became Professor in the History of Religions at Bergen (~1996).
Kobun Chino Otogawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1958–1962) and Kyoto University (~1962–1965). He later taught Reginald A. Ray.
Kodo Akino was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University and later served there as president (~1923–1925).
Hiromichi Kato is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ryogon Fukuhara as a graduate student. He served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University and taught Collett Cox.
Kodo Kawamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Komazawa University (~1952–1956) and later served as a professor there until 2003.
Kodo Sawaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Sotan Oka (~1908–1912). He later served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1935–1963).
Kodo Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who held teaching posts at Komazawa University and Keio University.

Koen Wellens works in Sinology, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Ghent University under Charles Willemen and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo (~-2006) under Per Kvaerne, with a committee including Signe Howell, Toni Huber, and Charles F. McKhann.
Koenraad Elst works in the fields of indology and religious studies. He studied at KU Leuven (~-1992, MA) and at Banaras Hindu University.

Kogen Mizuno studied indology and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1925–1928) and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1971). He held posts at Komazawa University (1935–1976), Keio University, and the University of Tokyo (1959–1962).

Kogi Kudara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University until 1979 and worked as an editor for the Ryukoku Association of Buddhist Studies in 2002.

Koichi Hokazono studied indology and Buddhist studies at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD from Kyushu University. He held posts at Kyushu University and served as a professor at The International University of Kagoshima until 1997.
